description: Veil of Summer's 'hexproof from blue and from black' granted mid-stack causes an already-cast opponent blue spell targeting the protected permanent to become illegal and be countered by the game rules on resolution - the deck's closest analogue to a 'protection' fixture (charter Gate 2 minimum list), since the subject deck's actual protection-adjacent cards are hexproof/ward rather than keyword protection.
artificial_state_elements: Cyclonic Rift (a real blue targeted spell not in the subject decklist) stands in for a generic opponent removal/bounce spell - any blue targeted spell aimed at the protected permanent works identically.
1 Forest is the minimum mana to cast Veil of Summer ({G}); no other board state modeled.
material_characteristics: Veil of Summer grants hexproof from blue and from black until end of turn, and can be cast at instant speed in response to a spell already on the stack
A spell that already has a target that becomes illegal for it loses that target under CR 608.2b, and if all its targets are illegal it doesn't resolve
abstracted_characteristics: Identity of the blue spell being fizzled - any targeted blue spell aimed at the now-hexproof permanent behaves identically
All board state not directly involved in the interaction

legal_actions: Cast Veil of Summer targeting no one (it targets nothing), granting seat 1 and their permanents hexproof from blue and from black until end of turn
illegal_actions_to_reject: Opponent casting a new blue spell targeting any of seat 1's permanents while the hexproof-from-blue effect is active - no legal target exists
expected.outcome_if_resolved: Veil of Summer resolves; Cyclonic Rift's only target (Delighted Halfling) becomes illegal; Cyclonic Rift is removed from the stack without effect under CR 608.2b and put into seat 2's graveyard.
